exposure: Maternal age (early teenage: 13-16 years, late teenage: 17-19 years, adult: 25-29 years)
outcome: Pregnancy risk factors (single marital status, rural living, living with extended family)
cohort: A sample of 395 pregnant teenagers and 736 pregnant adult women (25-29 years old) from an academic hospital.
finding: Adolescent mothers were more likely to have distinct social risk factors (e.g., being single, living in rural areas) and their newborns were more likely to be low birth weight.
mod_finding: Adolescent mothers were more likely to have a vaginal delivery and had a lower rate of operative delivery compared to adult mothers.
cross-section timing: Data collected during January 2011 and December 2012
birth_weight: Low birth weight was an outcome measured; 14.9% of newborns from adolescent mothers were low birth weight compared to 9.1% from adult mothers.
